aws-redshift-s3:position-deletes:v2.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): a DELETE writes position delete files and leaves the data files in place, confirmed from the Iceberg snapshot summary (delete-files=1, total-position-deletes=1, data files unchanged). Both directions, not read-only.
caveats: v3 tables record deletes as deletion vectors instead; a v3 table cannot add new positional delete files, though it can still read existing ones

aws-redshift-s3:position-deletes:v3.notes: Measured on Redshift Serverless 1.0.416217 (S3 buckets mode): both halves. A v3 DELETE removes the row positionally, encoded as a Puffin deletion vector with the data files left in place -- the Iceberg spec defines position deletes as encoded in a position delete file (v2) or a deletion vector (v3 and above), so a deletion vector is the v3 encoding of this feature rather than its absence. And a v2 table's position deletes still apply after an in-place upgrade to v3 via ALTER TABLE SET TABLE PROPERTIES, so legacy position delete files stay readable.
caveats: New positional delete *files* cannot be added to a v3 table; v3 records position deletes as deletion vectors instead
The in-place v2 to v3 upgrade is metadata-only and the deleted row stays absent afterwards, verified rather than assumed

links.label: Iceberg spec: row-level deletes

aws-redshift-s3:equality-deletes:v2.notes: Not supported as a write operation. Redshift's own writer produces position deletes, not equality deletes -- a measured DELETE reported total-equality-deletes=0 alongside total-position-deletes=1. It can read equality delete files written by another engine, but that read half is not verified by this suite: no engine in the harness writes equality delete files (Spark's DELETE either writes positional deletes or rewrites whole data files), so no fixture carrying equality deletes can be built. A Flink upsert sink with equality fields would be needed.
